report.headline: Elite-usage 18-year-old EuroLeague creator projected for an above-average but far narrower NBA role, with efficiency outlook unresolved

projection.text: Usage rate is projected at 23.7% in the NBA, above the league average of 20.0% but a clear step down from the 28.9% usage and +1.85 sd standing he carried in the EuroLeague; the fitted EL->NBA slope of 0.575 on usage means only about 57.5% of a player's standing above his source league typically carries over.

risks.text: Usage rate is projected to fall from 28.9% in the EuroLeague to 23.7% in the NBA, a drop of roughly one standard deviation of the receiving league's usage distribution (5.2%).

The true shooting projection of 55.2% should be treated with caution: the model's error on this metric (4.5% MAE) is worse than simply predicting the league mean (4.3% MAE) over 277 held-out transitions, so it carries no reliable information beyond the league's own scale.
The source-season sample is thin for an 18-year-old: only 33 games and 856 minutes, and the historical basis for this EL->NBA translation rests on just 61 prior transitions.

Players who make this move already sit +0.46 sd above their own league's average before any adjustment, meaning some of the gap over an average EuroLeague player reflects selection into the move rather than a translatable skill difference.

strengths.text: Elite offensive engagement in the EuroLeague: 22.2 points and 6.0 assists per 75 possessions with a 29.8% assist rate, while carrying a usage rate of 28.9% — 1.85 standard deviations above the EuroLeague average.
True shooting of 61.2%, itself 0.39 sd above the EuroLeague mean, was maintained on high volume, with half of all shot attempts coming from three.
Turnover rate was contained at 15.0% despite the heavy shot- and playmaking creation load implied by a 28.9% usage rate.

The usage rate projection of 23.7%, above the NBA average of 20.0%, comes from a model that beats the trivial league-mean baseline on this metric (3.2% MAE vs 4.2% MAE across 277 held-out transitions).

uncertainty.text: The 80% prediction interval for usage rate runs from 18.5% to 28.8%, a span of roughly 10 points — about two standard deviations of the NBA usage distribution — and the 95% interval widens to 15.8%-31.5%, so the model can indicate this is likely an above-average role but cannot pin down where within it he lands.
